question.problem:
Suppose $a=[5,\,3]^{T}$ and $b=[9,\,-9]^{T}.$ Find the Chebyshev distance between $a$ and $b.$

${d}_{\infty }(a,b)=$ {{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the Chebyshev distance is defined as

$$
{d}_{\infty }(a,b)=‖a-b{‖}_{\infty }
$$

where for an $N$-dimensional vector $v,$

$$
‖v{‖}_{\infty }=max(|{v}_{1}|,|{v}_{2}|,…,|{v}_{N}|).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{d}_{\infty }(a,b) & =‖a-b{‖}_{\infty } \\  & ={‖[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -9\end{aligned}]‖}_{\infty } \\  & =max(|5-9|,|3-(-9)|) \\  & =max(4,12) \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$
